lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: Tonight, we have a very special guest.
lines.cn: M：今晚我们有一位非常特别的嘉宾。

lines.t: M: Mrs.
lines.cn: 安娜·桑切斯夫人，

lines.t: M: Anna Sanchez is a three-time Olympic champion and author of the new book, To the Edge.
lines.cn: M：三次奥运会冠军，也是新书《致边缘》的作者。

lines.t: M: Mrs.
lines.cn: 桑切斯夫人，

lines.t: M: Sanchez, thank you for joining us.
lines.cn: M：谢谢您来参加节目。

lines.t: F: Thank you for having me.
lines.cn: F：谢谢你们邀请我。

lines.t: M: Let's start with your book.
lines.cn: M：我们从您的书开始吧。

lines.t: M: What does the title, To the Edge, mean?
lines.cn: M：《致边缘》这个书名是什么意思？

lines.t: M: What are you referring to?
lines.cn: M：您指的是什么？

lines.t: F: The book is about how science and technology has helped push humans to the edge of their physical abilities.
lines.cn: F：这本书讲的是科学技术如何推动人类逼近身体能力的极限。

lines.t: F: I argue that in the past 20 years, we have had the best athletes the world has ever seen.
lines.cn: F：我认为，过去 20 年里，我们拥有了有史以来最优秀的运动员。

lines.t: M: But is this a fair comparison?
lines.cn: M：但这样比较公平吗？

lines.t: M: How do you know how, say, a football player from 50 years ago would compare to one today?
lines.cn: M：你怎么知道 50 年前的足球运动员和今天的相比会怎样？

lines.t: F: Well, you are right.
lines.cn: F：嗯，你是对的。

lines.t: F: That comparison would be perhaps impossible to make.
lines.cn: F：那样的比较或许根本无法进行。

lines.t: F: But the point is more about our knowledge today of human biochemistry, nutrition, and mechanics.
lines.cn: F：但重点更多在于我们今天对人类生物化学、营养学和运动力学的了解。

lines.t: F: I believe that while our bodies have not changed in thousands of years, what has changed is the scientific knowledge.
lines.cn: F：我相信，虽然我们的身体几千年来并没有变化，变化的是科学知识。

lines.t: F: This has allowed athletes to push the limits of what was previously thought possible.
lines.cn: F：这让运动员得以突破过去被认为可能的极限。

lines.t: M: That's interesting.
lines.cn: M：有意思。

lines.t: M: Please tell us more about these perceived limits.
lines.cn: M：请多讲讲这些被认为是极限的东西。

lines.t: F: The world is seeing sports records being broken that could only be broken with the aid of technology, whether this be the speed of a tennis serve or the fastest time in a 100-meter dash or 200-meter swimming race.
lines.cn: F：世界正在见证一些只有借助技术才能打破的体育纪录，无论是网球发球的速度，还是 100 米短跑或 200 米游泳的最快时间。

lines.t: M: Is there any concern that technology is giving some athletes an unfair advantage over others?
lines.cn: M：有没有人担心，技术正在让一些运动员获得超越他人的不公平优势？

lines.t: F: That is an interesting question and one that has to be considered very carefully.
lines.cn: F：这是个有意思的问题，必须非常仔细地加以考虑。

lines.t: F: Skis, for example, went from being made of wood to a metal alloy, which allows for better control and faster speed.
lines.cn: F：例如滑雪板已从木质变成金属合金，这让控制更好、速度更快。

lines.t: F: There is no stopping technological progress, but, as I said, each situation should be considered carefully on a case-by-case basis.
lines.cn: F：技术进步无法阻挡，但正如我所说，每一种情况都应当逐案仔细权衡。

questions.stem: What does the woman think is required to be successful in international trade?

options.A: Experience.
options.B: Flexibility.
options.C: Family background.
options.D: Business connections.

questions.cn: 女士认为在国际贸易中取得成功需要什么？

optionsCn.C: 家庭背景。
optionsCn.D: 业务人脉。

questions.stem: What does the woman say is special about her way of doing trade?

options.A: Buying directly from factories.
options.B: Shipping goods in bulk by sea.
options.C: Having partners in many parts of the world.
options.D: Using the same container back and forth.

questions.cn: 女士说她做生意的方式有什么特别之处？

optionsCn.C: 在世界许多地方拥有伙伴。
optionsCn.D: 用同一个集装箱往返运输。

questions.stem: What does the woman have in both Italy and China?

options.A: Warehouses.
options.B: Factories.
options.C: Investors.
options.D: Retailers.

questions.cn: 女士在意大利和中国各有什么？

optionsCn.C: 投资者。
optionsCn.D: 零售商。

questions.stem: What does the woman say makes furniture marginally more profitable?

options.A: Trendy style.
options.B: Unique design.
options.C: Lower import duties.
options.D: Lower shipping costs.

questions.cn: 女士说什么使家具的利润率略高？

optionsCn.C: 更低的进口关税。
optionsCn.D: 更低的运输成本。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: F: I've worked in international trade all my life.
lines.cn: F：我一辈子都在做国际贸易。

lines.t: F: My father did so, too, before me, so I guess you could say it runs in the family.
lines.cn: F：我父亲在我之前也做这行，所以我想你可以说这是家传的。

lines.t: M: What products have you worked with?
lines.cn: M：你经手过哪些产品？

lines.t: F: All sorts, really.
lines.cn: F：其实什么都做过。

lines.t: F: I've imported textiles, machinery, toys, solar panels, all kinds of things over the years.
lines.cn: F：这些年我进口过纺织品、机械、玩具、太阳能板，各种东西。

lines.t: F: Trends and demand come and go, so one needs to be very flexible to succeed in this industry.
lines.cn: F：潮流和需求来来去去，所以要在这个行业成功，就必须非常灵活。

lines.t: M: I see.
lines.cn: M：我明白了。

lines.t: M: What goods are you trading now?
lines.cn: M：你现在做什么商品？

lines.t: F: I now import furniture from China into Italy and foods from Italy into China.
lines.cn: F：我现在把家具从中国进口到意大利，再把食品从意大利进口到中国。

lines.t: F: I even use the same container.
lines.cn: F：我甚至用同一个集装箱。

lines.t: F: It's a very efficient way of conducting trade.
lines.cn: F：这是非常高效的贸易方式。

lines.t: M: The same container?
lines.cn: M：同一个集装箱？

lines.t: M: You mean you own a 40-foot cargo container?
lines.cn: M：你是说你拥有一只 40 英尺的货柜？

lines.t: F: Yeah, that's right.
lines.cn: F：对，没错。

lines.t: F: I have a warehouse in Genova, Italy, and another in Shanghai.
lines.cn: F：我在意大利热那亚有一个仓库，在上海也有一个。

lines.t: F: I source mid-century modern furniture from different factories in China.
lines.cn: F：我从中国不同的工厂采购中世纪现代风格的家具。

lines.t: F: It's very good value for money.
lines.cn: F：它物超所值。

lines.t: F: I collect it all in my warehouse and then dispatch it to my other warehouse in Italy.
lines.cn: F：我把它们全部集中到我的仓库，然后发往我在意大利的另一个仓库。

lines.t: F: Over there, I do the same, but with Italian foods instead of furniture, things like pasta, cheese, wine, chocolates, and I send all that to my warehouse in China in the same freight container I use for the furniture.
lines.cn: F：在那边我做同样的事，只是把家具换成意大利食品，比如意面、奶酪、葡萄酒、巧克力，然后我用运家具的同一个货柜把这些全部发往我在中国的仓库。

lines.t: M: So I presume you sell both lines of products wholesale in each respective country.
lines.cn: M：那我猜，两种产品你都在各自的国家批发销售。

lines.t: F: Of course.
lines.cn: F：当然。

lines.t: F: I possess a network of clients and partners in both countries.
lines.cn: F：我在两个国家都拥有客户和合作伙伴网络。

lines.t: F: That's the main benefit of having done this for so long.
lines.cn: F：这是长期从事这行的主要好处。

lines.t: F: I've made great business contacts over time.
lines.cn: F：这是长期从事这行的主要好处。

lines.t: M: How many times do you ship?
lines.cn: F：多年来我积累了很好的业务人脉。

lines.t: F: I did 12 shipments last year, 18 this year, and I hope to grow to around 25 next year.
lines.cn: M：你一年发多少次货？

lines.t: F: That's both ways, there and back again.
lines.cn: F：去年我发了 12 次，今年 18 次，希望明年能增长到 25 次左右。

lines.t: F: Demand for authentic Italian food in China is growing rapidly, and similarly, sales of affordable yet stylish wooden furniture are also increasing in Italy.
lines.cn: F：这是双程的，去程和回程都算。

lines.t: F: Furniture is marginally more profitable, mostly because it enjoys lower customs duties.
lines.cn: F：中国对正宗意大利食品的需求在快速增长；同样，意大利对物美价廉的木质家具的销量也在上升。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about humor in the workplace?

options.A: It helps employees to reduce their stress.
options.B: It prevents employees from feeling bored.
options.C: It strengthens harmony among employees.
options.D: It helps employees to view things positively.

questions.cn: 关于职场中的幽默，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.C: 它增强员工之间的和谐。
optionsCn.D: 它帮助员工积极看待事物。

questions.stem: What does the study by Howard Polio show?

options.A: Weekends are conducive to reducing stress.
options.B: Humor is vital to interpersonal relationships.
options.C: All workers experience some emotional stress.
options.D: Humor can help workers excel at routine tasks.

questions.cn: 霍华德·波利奥的研究显示了什么？

options.B: Take the boss doll apart as long as they reassemble it.
options.C: Design and install stress-reducing gadgets.
options.D: Strike at the boss doll as hard as they like.

questions.cn: 柯达的员工在幽默室里能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 砸碎玩具以释放积压的怨恨。
optionsCn.B: 把老板玩偶拆开，只要能装回去。
optionsCn.C: 设计并安装减压玩具。
optionsCn.D: 随心所欲地殴打老板玩偶。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: Too many people view their jobs as a five-day prison from which they are paroled every Friday, says Joel Goodman, founder of the Humor Project, a humor consulting group in Saratoga Springs, New York.
lines.cn: 太多人把自己的工作看成一周五天的监狱，每周五才获假释。纽约州萨拉托加斯普林斯幽默咨询机构“幽默项目”的创始人乔尔·古德曼这样说。

lines.t: Humor unlocks the office prison because it lets adults bring some of their childlike spirit to the job.
lines.cn: 幽默打开了办公室这座监狱的大门，因为它让成年人把一部分童心带到工作中。

lines.t: According to Howard Polio, professor of psychology at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, an office with humor breaks is an office with satisfied and productive employees.
lines.cn: 据田纳西大学诺克斯维尔分校心理学教授霍华德·波利奥说，有幽默休息时间的办公室，其员工既满意又高效。

lines.t: Polio conducted a study that proved humor can help workers excel at routine production tasks.
lines.cn: 波利奥进行了一项研究，证明幽默能帮助员工在例行的生产任务中表现出色。

lines.t: Employees perform better when they have fun.
lines.cn: 员工开心时表现更好。

lines.t: In large corporations with a hierarchy of power, there is often no outlet for stress.
lines.cn: 在有权力等级的大型企业里，往往没有排解压力的出口。

lines.t: Every company needs underground ways of poking fun at the organization, says Lynn M.
lines.cn: 每家公司都需要有私下调侃组织的方式。圣路易斯圣玛丽健康中心的职场幽默讲师琳恩·M.

lines.t: Mark, a speaker on workplace humor for St.
lines.cn: 马克说。

lines.t: Mary's Health Center in St.
lines.cn: 柯达位于纽约罗切斯特的分公司找到了一种方法，让两万名员工释放压抑已久的怨恨。

lines.t: Louis.
lines.cn: 他们那间 1000 平方英尺的幽默室里有一个玩具店。

lines.t: Kodak's Rochester, New York branch discovered a way for its 20,000 employees to uncork their bottled-up resentments.
lines.cn: 在房间里众多减压玩具中，最吸引人的是一个四肢可拆卸的老板玩偶。

lines.t: Their 1,000-square-foot humor room features a toy store.
lines.cn: 员工可以把玩偶拆开，只要把手脚装回原位就行。

lines.t: Among the room's many stress-reducing gadgets, the main attraction is a boss doll with detachable arms and legs.
lines.cn: 平面印刷制作公司老板桑迪·科恩创建了“语录板”，记录人们在紧迫工期下说出的离谱话语。

lines.t: Employees can take the doll apart as long as they put its arms and legs back in place.
lines.cn: 科恩说，人在压力下会说傻话。

lines.t: Sandy Cohen, owner of a graphic print production business, created the Quote Board to document the bizarre phrases people say when under strict deadlines.
lines.cn: 现在我们只要彼此看看，说一句：这句该上语录板了。

lines.t: When you're under stress, you say stupid things, says Cohen.
lines.cn: 现在我们只要彼此看看，说一句：这句该上语录板了。

lines.t: Now we just look at each other and say, that's one for the Quote Board.
lines.cn: 如今一些团队甚至把它变成了固定的团队文化。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say has aroused public interest?

options.A: The recent finding of a changed gene in obese mice.
options.B: A breakthrough in understanding gene modification.
options.C: A newly discovered way for people to lose weight.
options.D: The self-repairing ability of a gene in obese mice.

questions.cn: 讲话者说什么激起了公众的兴趣？

optionsCn.A: 在肥胖小鼠身上发现变异基因这一最新发现。
optionsCn.B: 在理解基因改造上的突破。
optionsCn.C: 一种新发现的人们减肥的方法。
optionsCn.D: 肥胖小鼠体内基因的自我修复能力。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the changed gene?

options.A: It renders an organism unable to fight diseases.
options.B: It prevents the mice's fatty tissues from growing.
options.C: It helps organisms adapt to environmental changes.
options.D: It renders mice unable to sense when to stop eating.

questions.cn: 关于那个变异基因，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它使机体无法对抗疾病。
optionsCn.B: 它阻止小鼠脂肪组织生长。
optionsCn.C: 它帮助机体适应环境变化。
optionsCn.D: 它使小鼠无法察觉何时该停止进食。

questions.stem: What does University of Vermont psychologist Esther Rothblum say?

options.A: Human beings have more obesity genes than most mice do.
options.B: Half of a person's total weight variation can be controlled.
options.C: People are born with a tendency to have a certain weight.
options.D: The function of the obesity genes is yet to be explored.

questions.cn: 佛蒙特大学心理学家埃丝特·罗思布卢姆说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 人类比大多数小鼠有更多肥胖基因。
optionsCn.B: 一个人总体体重差异的一半是可控的。
optionsCn.C: 人天生就带有倾向某个体重的特质。
optionsCn.D: 肥胖基因的功能尚待探索。

questions.stem: What accounts for Americans' obesity according to a survey by the Center for Disease Control?

options.A: The worsening of the natural environment.
options.B: The abundant provision of rich foods.
options.C: The accelerated pace of present-day life.
options.D: The adverse impact of the food industry.

questions.cn: 根据疾病控制中心的一项调查，是什么造成了美国人的肥胖？

optionsCn.C: 当今生活节奏的加快。
optionsCn.D: 食品业的不利影响。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: Public interest was aroused by the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice.
lines.cn: 在肥胖小鼠身上发现的一种发生变异的基因，激起了公众的兴趣。

lines.t: The news was made known by Rockefeller University geneticist Jeffrey Friedman.
lines.cn: 这一消息由洛克菲勒大学的遗传学家杰弗里·弗里德曼公布。

lines.t: The researchers believe this gene influences development of a hormone that tells the organism how fat or full it is.
lines.cn: 研究者相信，这个基因影响一种激素的发育，而这种激素告诉机体它有多胖或是否吃饱了。

lines.t: Those with the changed gene may not sense when they have eaten enough or if they have sufficient fatty tissue and thus can't tell when to stop eating.
lines.cn: 携带变异基因的个体可能察觉不到自己已经吃饱或脂肪是否充足，因此无法判断何时停止进食。

lines.t: The researchers also reported finding a gene nearly identical to the mouse obesity gene in humans.
lines.cn: 研究者还报告说，在人类身上发现了一个与小鼠肥胖基因几乎相同的基因。

lines.t: The operation of this gene in humans has not yet been demonstrated, however.
lines.cn: 然而，这个基因在人体内的作用尚未得到证实。

lines.t: Still, professionals like University of Vermont psychologist Esther Rothblum reacted enthusiastically.
lines.cn: 尽管如此，佛蒙特大学心理学家埃丝特·罗思布卢姆等专业人士反应热烈。

lines.t: This research indicates that people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight.
lines.cn: 这项研究表明，人确实天生就有倾向于某个体重的特质。

lines.t: Just as they are to have a particular skin color or height.
lines.cn: 就像天生具有特定肤色或身高一样。

lines.t: Actually, behavioral geneticists believe that less than half of the total weight variation is programmed in the genes while height is almost entirely genetically determined.
lines.cn: 实际上，行为遗传学家认为，总体体重差异中只有不到一半是由基因决定的，而身高则几乎完全由基因决定。

lines.t: Whatever role genes play, Americans are getting fatter.
lines.cn: 无论基因扮演什么角色，美国人正在变胖。

lines.t: A survey by the Center for Disease Control found that obesity has increased greatly over the last 10 years.
lines.cn: 美国疾病控制中心的一项调查发现，过去 10 年里肥胖大幅增加。

lines.t: Such rapid change underlines the role of environmental factors like the abundance of rich foods in Americans' overeating.
lines.cn: 如此快速的变化凸显了环境因素——比如丰富食物的充足供应——在美国人暴饮暴食中的作用。

lines.t: The Center for Disease Control has also found that teens are far less physically active than they were even a decade ago.
lines.cn: 疾病控制中心还发现，青少年的身体活动量远低于仅仅十年前。

lines.t: Accepting that weight is predetermined can relieve guilt for overweight people, but people's belief that they cannot control their weight can itself contribute to obesity.
lines.cn: 接受“体重早已注定”可以减轻超重者的负罪感，但“自己无法控制体重”这一信念本身，也可能助长肥胖。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What quality do men value most concerning friendship, according to a questionnaire response?

options.A: Similarity in interests.
options.B: Mental stimulation.
options.C: Openness.
options.D: Compassion.

questions.cn: 根据一份问卷回答，男性最看重友谊中的哪种品质？

optionsCn.C: 坦诚。
optionsCn.D: 体恤。

questions.stem: What do women refer to when speaking of close friendships?

options.A: The willingness to offer timely help.
options.B: The joy found in each other's company.
options.C: Personal bonds.
options.D: Emotional factors.

questions.cn: 女性谈到亲密友谊时指的是什么？

optionsCn.B: 彼此陪伴中找到的快乐。
optionsCn.C: 个人纽带。
optionsCn.D: 情感因素。

questions.stem: What may threaten a friendship for both men and women?

options.A: Failure to keep a promise.
options.B: Lack of frankness.
options.C: Feelings of betrayal.
options.D: Loss of contact.

questions.cn: 什么可能威胁男性和女性的友谊？

optionsCn.C: 被背叛的感觉。
optionsCn.D: 失去联系。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Qualities of a relationship such as openness, compassion, and mental stimulation are of concern to most of us regardless of sex.
lines.cn: 亲密关系的品质——比如坦诚、体恤和精神上的启发——是不分性别、我们大多数人都会关心的事。

lines.t: But, judging from the questionnaire response, they are more important to women than to men.
lines.cn: 但从问卷回答来看，这些品质对女性比对男性更重要。

lines.t: Asked to consider the ingredients of close friendship, women rated these qualities above all others.
lines.cn: 被要求考虑亲密友谊的要素时，女性把这些品质排在所有其他因素之上。

lines.t: Men assigned a lower priority to them in favor of similarity in interests, selected by 77 % of men, and responsiveness in a crisis, chosen by 61% of male respondents.
lines.cn: 男性对它们的排序较低，而更看重兴趣的相似性（77% 的男性选择）和危机时刻的响应（61% 的男性受访者选择）。

lines.t: Mental stimulation, ranked third in popularity by men as well as women, was the only area of overlap.
lines.cn: 精神启发在男性和女性中都排第三，是唯一重合的领域。

lines.t: Among men, only 28% named openness as an important quality Caring was picked by just 23%.
lines.cn: 在男性中，只有 28% 认为坦诚是重要品质；选择“关怀”的仅 23%。

lines.t: It is evident by their selections that when women speak of close friendships, they are referring to emotional factors, while men emphasize the pleasure they find in a friend's company.
lines.cn: 从他们的选择可以明显看出：当女性谈到亲密友谊时，她们指的是情感因素；而男性强调的是从朋友陪伴中得到的快乐。

lines.t: That is, when a man speaks of a friend, he is likely to be talking about someone he does things with, a teammate, a fellow hobbyist, a drinking buddy.
lines.cn: 也就是说，当一个男人说到朋友时，他很可能指的是一个和他一起做事的人：队友、同好、酒友。

lines.t: These activities are the fabric of the friendship.
lines.cn: 这些活动构成了友谊的骨架。

lines.t: It is a doing relationship, in which similarity in interests is the key bond.
lines.cn: 这是一种“一起做事”的关系，其中兴趣的相似是关键纽带。

lines.t: This factor was a consideration of less than 11% of women.
lines.cn: 只有不到 11% 的女性会考虑这一因素。

lines.t: Women opt for a warm, emotional atmosphere where communication flows freely.
lines.cn: 女性选择温暖、有情感交流的氛围，沟通在其中自由流动。

lines.t: Activity is mere background.
lines.cn: 活动只是背景。

lines.t: Lastly, men, as we have seen, have serious questions about each other's loyalty.
lines.cn: 最后，正如我们所见，男性对彼此的忠诚存在严重的疑虑。

lines.t: Perhaps this is why they placed such strong emphasis on responsiveness in a crisis.
lines.cn: 也许这就是他们如此强调危机时刻响应能力的原因。

lines.t: Someone I can call on for help.
lines.cn: 一个我求助时能找到的人。

lines.t: Women, as their testimonies indicate, are generally more secure with each other, and consequently are more likely to treat this issue lightly.
lines.cn: 正如她们的表述所显示的，女性彼此之间通常更有安全感，因此更可能轻描淡写地看待这个问题。

lines.t: In follow-up interviews, this was confirmed numerous times, as woman after woman indicated that being there when needed was taken for granted.
lines.cn: 在后续访谈中这一点被多次证实：一位又一位女性表示，需要时在场是理所当然的。

lines.t: As for the hazards of friendship, more than a few relationships have been shattered because of cutthroat competition and feelings of betrayal.
lines.cn: 至于友谊的风险，不少关系因你死我活的竞争和被背叛的感觉而破碎。

lines.t: This applies to both men and women, but unequally.
lines.cn: 这对男性和女性都适用，但程度不等。

lines.t: In comparison, nearly twice as many men complained about these issues as women.
lines.cn: 相比之下，男性抱怨这些问题的数量几乎是女性的两倍。

lines.t: Further, while competition and betrayal are the main thorns to female friendship, men are plagued in almost equal amounts by two additional issues, lack of frankness and a fear of appearing unmanly.
lines.cn: 此外，竞争和背叛是女性友谊的主要刺；而男性几乎同样程度地被另外两个问题困扰：缺乏坦诚，以及害怕显得不够男人。

lines.t: Obviously, for a man, a good friendship is hard to find.
lines.cn: 显然，对一个男人来说，好的友谊难寻。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: Where can many of the best dinosaur specimens be found in North America?

options.A: Along the low-lying Colorado River.
options.B: At the Dinosaur National Monument.
options.C: Along the border of the U.S. and Canada.
options.D: At museums of natural history in large cities.

questions.cn: 在北美，许多最好的恐龙标本可以在哪里看到？

optionsCn.C: 沿美国与加拿大边境。
optionsCn.D: 在大城市的自然历史博物馆。

questions.stem: What occurs to many people when they see the massive bones in the pit wall?

options.A: Volcanic explosions could bring whole animal species to extinction.
options.B: Some natural disasters killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in the area.
options.C: The pit should be carefully preserved for the study of dinosaurs.
options.D: The whole region must have been struck by a devastating flood.

questions.cn: 当人们看到坑壁上的大量骨骼时，会产生什么想法？

optionsCn.A: 火山爆发可能使整个物种灭绝。
optionsCn.B: 某些自然灾害杀死了该地区的一整群恐龙。
optionsCn.C: 应该为研究恐龙而精心保护这个坑。
optionsCn.D: 整个地区一定遭受过毁灭性洪水。

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest about the large number of dinosaur bones found in the pit?

options.A: They floated down an eastward flowing river.
options.B: They lay buried deep in the sand for millions of years.
options.C: They were skeletons of dinosaurs inhabiting the locality.
options.D: They were remains of dinosaurs killed in a volcanic explosion.

questions.cn: 关于坑中发现的大量恐龙骨骼，讲话者的观点是什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们沿一条东流的河漂了下来。
optionsCn.B: 它们在沙里深埋了数百万年。
optionsCn.C: 它们是栖息当地的恐龙的骨骼。
optionsCn.D: 它们是死于火山爆发的恐龙遗骸。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: The partial skeletons of more than 20 dinosaurs and the scattered bones of about 300 more have been discovered in Utah and Colorado at what is now the Dinosaur National Monument.
lines.cn: 在犹他州和科罗拉多州、如今的恐龙国家纪念公园，发现了 20 多具不完整的恐龙骨架，以及约 300 具恐龙散落的骨骼。

lines.t: Many of the best specimens may be seen today at museums of natural history in the largest cities of the United States and Canada.
lines.cn: 许多最好的标本如今可以在美国和加拿大最大城市的自然历史博物馆里看到。

lines.t: This dinosaur pit is the largest and best-preserved deposit of dinosaurs known today.
lines.cn: 这个恐龙坑是当今已知的规模最大、保存最好的恐龙堆积层。

lines.t: Many people get the idea from the mass of bones in the pit wall that some disaster such as a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in this area.
lines.cn: 许多人从坑壁上那堆骨骼得到一个想法：某种灾难——比如火山爆发或突如其来的洪水——杀死了这个地区的一整群恐龙。

lines.t: This could have happened, but it probably did not.
lines.cn: 这有可能，但多半不是。

lines.t: The main reasons for thinking otherwise are the scattered bones and the thickness of the deposit.
lines.cn: 不这么想的主要理由是那些散落的骨骼和堆积层的厚度。

lines.t: In other deposits where the animals were thought to have died together, the skeletons were usually complete and often all the bones were in their proper places.
lines.cn: 在其他被认为是动物群体死亡的地层中，骨架通常完整，骨骼常常都在原来的位置上。

lines.t: Rounded pieces of fossil bone have been found here.
lines.cn: 而这里发现的是被磨圆的化石骨块。

lines.t: These fragments got their smooth round shape by rolling along the stream bottom.
lines.cn: 这些碎块光滑浑圆的形状，是它们沿河床滚动形成的。

lines.t: In a mass killing, the bones would have been left on the stream or lake bottom together at the same level.
lines.cn: 如果是集体死亡，骨骼应当一同留在河床或湖底的同一层面上。

lines.t: But in this deposit, the bones occur throughout a zone of sandstone about 12 feet thick.
lines.cn: 但在这个堆积层里，骨骼分布在约 12 英尺厚的整个砂岩层中。

lines.t: The mixture of swamp dwellers and dry land types also seems to indicate that the deposit is a mixture from different places.
lines.cn: 沼泽栖居者与陆地物种混杂在一起，也似乎表明这一堆积层是来自不同地方的混合体。

lines.t: The pit area is a large dinosaur graveyard, not a place where they died.
lines.cn: 这个坑区是一座大型的恐龙墓地，而不是它们死亡的地方。

lines.t: Most of the remains probably floated down an eastward flowing river until they were left on a shallow sandbar.
lines.cn: 大部分遗骸可能沿一条东流的河漂来，直到搁浅在一片浅滩上。

lines.t: Some of them may have come from far away dry land areas to the west.
lines.cn: 其中一些可能来自西边很远的干旱陆地。

lines.t: Perhaps they drowned trying to cross a small stream or were washed away during floods.
lines.cn: 它们或许是在试图渡过一条小溪时淹死，或在洪水中被冲走。

lines.t: Some of the swamp dwellers may have got stuck in the very sandbar that became their grave.
lines.cn: 一些沼泽栖居者可能就卡在了后来成为它们坟墓的那片沙洲上。

lines.t: Others may have floated for miles before being stranded.
lines.cn: 其他的则可能漂流了数英里才搁浅。

lines.t: Even today, similar events take place.
lines.cn: 即使在今天，类似的事件仍在发生。

lines.t: When floods come in the spring, sheep, cattle and deer are often trapped by rising waters and often drown.
lines.cn: 当洪水在春季来临时，羊、牛和鹿常常被上涨的水困住，常常被淹死。

lines.t: Their dead bodies float downstream until the flood recedes and leaves them stranded on a bar or shore where they lie half buried in the sand until they decay.
lines.cn: 它们的尸体顺流漂下，直到洪水退去，把它们留在沙洲或岸边，半埋在沙里，直至腐烂。

lines.t: Early travelers on the Missouri River reported that shores and bars were often lined with the decaying bodies of buffalo that had died during spring floods.
lines.cn: 早期在密苏里河上旅行的人报告说，河岸和沙洲上常常排满春洪中死去的野牛腐烂的尸体。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What have young Americans been accused of?

options.A: Indulging in seeking leisure and material comfort.
options.B: Attaching too much importance to independence.
options.C: Failing to care for parents in the traditional way.
options.D: Leaving their parents on the verge of starvation.

questions.cn: 美国年轻人被指责什么？

optionsCn.A: 沉溺于追求休闲和物质享受。
optionsCn.C: 未能以传统方式照顾父母。
optionsCn.D: 任由父母濒临挨饿。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about old people in the United States?

options.A: They have great difficulty living by themselves.
options.B: They have little hope of getting any family care.
options.C: They have fond memories of their good old days.
options.D: They have a sense of independence and autonomy.

questions.cn: 关于美国的老年人，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们自己生活有很大困难。
optionsCn.B: 他们几乎没有得到家人照顾的希望。
optionsCn.C: 他们对过去的好日子怀有美好回忆。
optionsCn.D: 他们有独立与自主的意识。

questions.stem: What is astonishing to the young mothers interviewed by the speaker?

options.A: People in many parts of the world preferred small-size families.
options.B: There have been extended families in most parts of the world.
options.C: Many elderly people were unwilling to take care of their grandchildren.
options.D: So many young Americans refused to live together with their parents.

questions.cn: 令受访的年轻妈妈们吃惊的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 世界许多地方的人更喜欢小家庭。
optionsCn.B: 世界大部分地区存在大家庭。
optionsCn.C: 许多老年人不愿意照顾孙辈。
optionsCn.D: 这么多美国年轻人拒绝与父母同住。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say older people try their best to do?

options.A: Leave their younger generations alone.
options.B: Avoid being a burden to their children.
options.C: Stay healthy by engaging in joyful activities.
options.D: View things from their children's perspective.

questions.cn: 讲话者说老年人竭尽全力想做到什么？

optionsCn.C: 通过参加快乐的活动保持健康。
optionsCn.D: 从孩子的角度看事情。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: I would like particularly to talk about the need to develop a new style of aging in our own society.
lines.cn: 我特别想谈的是，我们自己的社会需要发展出一种新的老龄化模式。

lines.t: Young people in this country have been accused of not caring for their parents the way they would have in the old country.
lines.cn: 有人指责这个国家的年轻人不像从前在故国那样照顾自己的父母。

lines.t: And this is true.
lines.cn: 这是事实。

lines.t: But it is also true that old people have been influenced by an American ideal of independence and autonomy.
lines.cn: 但同样属实的是：老年人也受到了美国式独立自主理想的影响。

lines.t: So we live alone, perhaps on the verge of starvation, in time without friends, but we are independent.
lines.cn: 于是我们独自生活，可能濒临挨饿，一段时间没有朋友，但我们是独立的。

lines.t: This standard American style has been forced on every ethnic group, although there are many groups for whom the ideal is not practical.
lines.cn: 这种标准的美式模式被强加给每一个族群，尽管对许多族群而言这一理想并不现实。

lines.t: It is a poor ideal, and pursuing it does a great deal of harm.
lines.cn: 这是个糟糕的理想，追求它造成巨大的伤害。

lines.t: This ideal of independence also contains a tremendous amount of unselfishness.
lines.cn: 这种独立理想还包含了大量的“无私”。

lines.t: In talking to today's young mothers, I have asked them what kind of grandmothers they think they are going to be.
lines.cn: 在和如今的年轻妈妈们交谈时，我问她们，觉得自己将来会做怎样的祖母。

lines.t: I hear devoted, loving mothers say that when they are through raising their children, they have no intention of becoming grandmothers.
lines.cn: 我听到一些尽心尽力的慈爱母亲说，等把孩子养大，她们不打算当祖母。

lines.t: They are astonished to hear that in most of the world, throughout most of its history, families have been three- or four-generation families, living under the same roof.
lines.cn: 当她们听说，在世界大多数地方、在大部分历史中，家庭都是三四代人同住一个屋檐下时，她们非常吃惊。

lines.t: We have overemphasized the small family unit, father, mother, small children.
lines.cn: 我们过度强调了小家庭单元：父亲、母亲、小孩子。

lines.t: We think it is wonderful if grandma and grandpa, if they're still alive, can live alone.
lines.cn: 我们觉得，如果爷爷奶奶还健在，能独立生活就很好。

lines.t: We have reached the point where we think the only thing we can do for our children is to stay out of their way, and the only thing we can do for our daughter-in-law is to see as little of her as possible.
lines.cn: 我们已经到了这种地步：认为我们能为孩子做的唯一一件事，就是不妨碍他们；能为儿媳做的唯一一件事，就是尽量少和她见面。

lines.t: Old people's nursing homes, even the best run, are filled with older people who believe the only thing they can do for their children is to look cheerful when they come to visit.
lines.cn: 老年人疗养院——哪怕是经营得最好的——里面都是这样的老人：他们相信，自己能为孩子做的唯一一件事，就是当他们来探望时显得愉快。

lines.t: So in the end, older people have to devote all their energies to not being a burden.
lines.cn: 于是到最后，老年人不得不把全部精力都用于“不成为负担”。

lines.t: We are beginning to see what a tremendous price we've paid for our emphasis on independence and autonomy.
lines.cn: 我们开始看到，为强调独立与自主，我们付出了多么巨大的代价。

lines.t: We've isolated old people, and we've cut off the children from their grandparents.
lines.cn: 我们把老年人孤立起来，也切断了孩子与祖辈的联系。

lines.t: One of the reasons we have as bad a generation gap today as we do is that grandparents have stepped out.
lines.cn: 如今代沟之所以如此严重，一个原因就是祖辈退出了。

lines.t: Young people are being deprived of the thing they need most, perspective, to know why their parents behave so peculiarly and why their grandparents say the things they do.
lines.cn: 年轻人正被剥夺他们最需要的东西——一种纵览的视角：明白父母为何表现得那么怪异，祖辈为何说那些话。
